result.keyword: Who are the best workers compensation lawyers in Melbourne?
result.markdown:
If you mean **lawyers representing injured workers in Melbourne (rather than employers/insurers)**, the strongest current shortlist is fairly clear.

### My top picks

1. **Maurice Blackburn Personal Injury Lawyers Melbourne** — **best overall**
   - Doyle’s Guide ranks Maurice Blackburn **First Tier** for Victorian plaintiff work-injury compensation in 2026.
   - Several individual Maurice Blackburn lawyers are also ranked **Preeminent**, including Lachlan Fitch, Patricia McMullan and Ross Sottile. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - Particularly strong if your matter could progress beyond ordinary weekly benefits into **serious injury/common-law compensation**.

2. **Slater and Gordon Lawyers** — **best for a large specialist team**
   - Also **First Tier** in Doyle's 2026 ranking.
   - Rod Matthews, Alisha Muscara and Nimna Rupasinghe are among its lawyers recognised in the current rankings. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - They specifically handle Melbourne WorkCover claims and have offices throughout Melbourne. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/workers-compensation/workers-compensation-lawyers-in-melbourne?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

3. **Zaparas Lawyers** — **best specialist-focused alternative**
   - **First Tier** in Doyle's 2026 ranking.
   - Peter Zaparas, Yianni Zaparas and Mark Mitchell are all listed as **Preeminent** workers' compensation lawyers. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - Strong choice for complicated claims, impairment disputes, serious injuries and common-law claims.

4. **Gordon Legal Melbourne** — **excellent boutique/medium-size option**
   - Doyle's places Gordon Legal in the **Second Tier** for Victorian plaintiff work-injury compensation. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
   - Worth considering if you prefer a more specialised personal-injury practice without going to one of the very largest firms.

5. **Arnold Dallas McPherson Injury Lawyers Melbourne** — **strong specialist alternative**
   - Doyle's places the firm in the **Third Tier**, with John McPherson recognised as **Preeminent** in the individual lawyer rankings. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### If it were my shortlist

I'd get **three initial opinions**, probably:

**Zaparas + Maurice Blackburn + Slater & Gordon.**

They're the three firms currently in **Doyle's First Tier**, and importantly, that ranking is based on peer nominations/interviews rather than firms simply paying to appear. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-lawyers-plaintiff-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/work-injury-compensation-law-firms-victoria/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

One important distinction: **the best firm depends heavily on what stage your claim is at.** A straightforward rejected WorkCover claim is different from a permanent impairment claim or a serious-injury/common-law claim. In Victoria, a serious injury caused by someone else's negligence can potentially support a common-law damages claim for pain and suffering and/or economic loss. [www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/common-law-claim-damages?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Also, if you're simply disputing a WorkCover decision, the **Workplace Injury Commission provides a free conciliation process**, and WorkSafe says applications generally need to be lodged within **60 days of the decision letter**. [www.worksafe.vic.gov.au](https://www.worksafe.vic.gov.au/get-help-decision-about-your-workcover-claim?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me **what happened (e.g. back injury, psychological injury, rejected claim, employer dispute, permanent impairment, or serious injury) and roughly when it happened**, I can narrow this down to the **best 2–3 Melbourne lawyers/firms for your particular case**, including who I'd call first.
